findings.finding: decide_gate's all_generated success branch was checked before the waiver-consumption-failure branch. A PR whose only changed path is a corroborated review-record file (.shipwright/planning/iterate/<run>/reviews.json, itself is_generated_path) can have all_generated=True and needs_review=False at once; if the waiver-consumption step then fails, the all_generated branch matched first and posted success, masking the failure test_failed_waiver_consumption_cannot_post_a_green_gate exists to prevent.
findings.suggestion: Reorder the waiver-consumption-failure check before the all_generated short-circuit; add a regression test combining all_generated=True with needs_review=False and waiver_consumed_ok=False.

findings.finding: classify_generated_only's reuse of is_generated_path is a safe carve-out for any combination of changed paths that classifier accepts
the basename-only matches (triage.jsonl, shipwright_events.jsonl, etc.) are an acceptable input to a full review-skip decision
decide_gate's test/docstring treat 'timed_out' as a real GitHub Actions step outcome value

GitHub Actions `run:` steps default to `bash -e -o pipefail`. If `decide_pr_review_gate.py` exits non-zero (argparse error, missing module, uv failure), the `gate_out=$(...)` assignment aborts the step before the `state`/`desc` guard and before the `gh api` status post. The carefully-written "gate decision script produced no output" fallback is unreachable for the crash case it claims to cover — a crash now results in no posted status instead of the previous guaranteed `failure` status, weakening the "one producer, always posts" invariant (hard constraint 3/4).
findings.suggestion: Capture the failure explicitly, e.g. `gate_out=$(uv run ... ) || gate_out=""`, so the existing empty-state guard actually fires and a `failure` status is still posted.

findings.finding: The spec requires the tier step to emit new outputs `all_generated` / `all_generated_reason` to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`, but the diff shows only a comment addition to that step — no change to the bash that writes step outputs. If the existing output-capture logic is not a generic key=value passthrough of the tool's stdout, `steps.tier.outputs.all_generated` will be empty, the review step's `if:` still passes (`'' != 'true'`), review runs, and — because `REVIEW_OUTCOME` would be `success`/`failure` — the all-generated branch never fires. The change silently no-ops instead of failing loudly. The new shape test (`test_generated_only_gate_derived_from_api_changed_paths`) only checks the consumer side of the wiring, so a missing producer would pass all tests.
findings.suggestion: Add a shape assertion that the tier step actually writes `all_generated` to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` (or show the capture is a generic passthrough), e.g. assert `all_generated= >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"` or equivalent in `test_pr_review_workflow_shape.py`.

findings.finding: An all-generated PR that is also waived (`needs_review=False`, waiver consumed OK) posts `all_generated_reason` instead of the historical `tier_reason` — the "ordinary waived PRs keep their exact original descriptions" ledger row is only tested for `all_generated=False`. Minor behavioral drift, arguably intended, but untested and unstated.
findings.suggestion: Either add a test pinning the intended description for the all-generated + waived + waiver-ok combination, or note it in the docstring.

findings.finding: The regex extracting the review step's `if:` bounds it by `\n\senv:` and a 300-char window. It asserts the `all_generated != 'true'` clause exists but not that the original two conditions remain — a future edit dropping `needs_review == 'true'` from the `if:` would still pass this test. Combined with the missing producer-side assertion above, the workflow-shape coverage of the new gating is thinner than the ledger implies.
findings.suggestion: Assert all three conditions of the `if:` are present.  Non-findings I checked and consider sound: `decide_gate` branch ordering matches the spec (waiver-failure before the all-generated short-circuit, per the Stage-2 review fix); sensitive-path and truncated/empty-list handling in `classify_generated_only` are correct; `is_safe_to_skip_review`'s narrowing (agent-docs exclusion, canonical basename anchoring) is implemented and well-tested; no shell-injection risk in the new arg passing (all quoted, sed parsing is non-eval).  Overall: the core logic and tests are solid, but the workflow wiring has two real gaps — the crash-path guard is dead code under default `bash -e`, and the tier-step output producer is never verified — both of which could make the carve-out silently inert or change the posted-status guarantee. Ship-with-fixes.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
